### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**20** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 44ccf94a409362dbb3c16fc2f03b321d4e91b797` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d1e154884bcb9e32cbc473b6e3f1f297fc746b05` — the merge of head `620499a87efcac52eb3f6c413a7c30a2c3268041` into base `44ccf94a409362dbb3c16fc2f03b321d4e91b797`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d1e154884bcb9e32cbc473b6e3f1f297fc746b05 && git checkout d1e154884bcb9e32cbc473b6e3f1f297fc746b05
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 44ccf94a409362dbb3c16fc2f03b321d4e91b797 620499a87efcac52eb3f6c413a7c30a2c3268041 && git checkout -B drift-repro 44ccf94a409362dbb3c16fc2f03b321d4e91b797 && git merge --no-ff 620499a87efcac52eb3f6c413a7c30a2c3268041

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 44ccf94a409362dbb3c16fc2f03b321d4e91b797
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `620499a87efcac52eb3f6c413a7c30a2c3268041`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/own-door-bridge.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/approvals.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-hooks.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/comments.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/webhooks.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/own-door-bridge.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-hooks.test.ts, scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs

Inputs read: card #37737 (body and both comments), PR #37813 (body, 13 files, net diff against `main`), and the check-runs on this head: 58 success, 11 skipped, none failed. `Test UI (12/16)` is green after the one re-run the seat recorded on the PR. Code outside the diff was read on `origin/main` at `c826e8a15`; none of the touched files changed on `main` since the PR's base `44ccf94a4`.

The rest of the diff is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`: the changeset and the three other test files (`approvals-act.test.ts`, `comments.test.ts` and `webhooks-redeliver.test.ts`).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Wire: ten `501` answers gain `Vary: Accept-Language`.** Right. These are the bridge's two and the eight of the comment, webhook-redelivery, approval action-page and inbound-hook doors. Status, `code` and body are unchanged. On `main` these ten are the only `501`s whose sentence follows the request's language (every `requestLocaleOf` reader in `packages/runtime`), so "every door that answers a localized `501` answers through this" holds.
- **The header reaches the client.** Right. Both senders copy `response.headers`: `packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts:846` and `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts:485`. Hono 4.13.18's `cors` appends `Vary: Origin` after the handler, and the compression middleware appends `Accept-Encoding` to an existing `Vary`, so neither member replaces the other.
- **The header is complete.** Right. `requestLocaleOf` reads `Accept-Language` and nothing else, and the header is sent on the English answer too.
- **Two `ja-JP` sentences change (`受信オートメーションフック` to `受信自動化フック`).** Right. No other file on `main` uses `オートメーション`; the `ui/packages/i18n` and `platform-objects` Japanese bundles say `自動化`. The English is untouched.
- **No package export changes.** Right. `localizedNotImplemented` and `catalogNotImplemented` are exported from `own-door-bridge.ts`, which `packages/runtime/src/index.ts` does not re-export.
- **The gate row `own-door-bridge.ts` goes from `handBuilt: 0` to `1` with a note.** Right. It is the gate's own kind 1 (`deps.error` takes no headers), and the four door modules stay at `0`.
- **The noun pin tightens to `/\bdoors?$/`, and the plural flag to `/\bdoors$/`.** Right. The three shipped nouns pass, and a plural noun spelled another way now fails.
- **`Fixes #37737`.** Items 1 to 4 are delivered in the tree. Item 5 is card #37811 (open, `Blocked-by: #37737`). Item 6 is delivered for the `501`s only; see S1.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/runtime` patch and `@objectstack/spec` patch match what the diff publishes: one response header on existing `501` answers, two catalog strings, and doc comments. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right, because nothing an author can write changes. `Clause-②: no` is right: no accept set moves, no export is added to a package entry point, and the header adds no field a client must send or parse. Both lines are in the PR body and the changeset. `Check Changeset` is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag "Vary goes only on the `501`s, not on the whole envelope".** The call holds for the ten `501`s. Its stated premise does not hold for the rest, and it is escalated as S1.
- **Dev flag "item 4 is closed by widening".** Answered: the walk and the pin are both wider in the tree. See N3 for what the walk still cannot see.
- **`open_questions`.** The PR body carries none.
- **SQL push-down.** The diff reads and writes no data, so there is nothing to push down.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts` (hits).** The two rewritten jsdoc passages agree with the resolver on `main`. The catalog holds `en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP` and `es-ES`. Read through `resolveLocaleAmong` (`i18n-resolver.ts:678`): `es-MX` reaches `es-ES` at step 5, `zh` and `ja` reach `zh-CN` and `ja-JP` at step 3, `zh-TW` finds no Traditional key at step 3 and reaches `zh-CN` at step 5, and `fr` or `de` match nothing, so `operationUserMessage` drops the locale and the renderer answers English. The print door reads the same way (`print-routes.ts:321`, then `operationUserMessage`), so "as the print door's is" is true. The first consumer of the `ja-JP` strings is `automation-hooks.ts` through `catalogNotImplemented`, and `automation-hooks.test.ts` pins both sentences per language.

**Implementing files.** `localizedNotImplemented` spreads `deps.error`'s envelope and adds the one header; `catalogNotImplemented` renders the key exactly as each door did before (`operationUserMessage(key, { locale: requestLocaleOf(context) })`). The eight call sites pass the same keys as before, so no sentence moves. The `noun` jsdoc and the test agree. I tried to break it four ways and none held: a host `Vary` being overwritten (see ①), an English answer without the header (pinned), a non-localized answer gaining it (the miss and the `500`s still go through `deps.routeNotFound` and `deps.error`), and a door bypassing the helper (none on `main`).

S1 (should-fix) — Item 6 of the card closes on a premise the tree contradicts. The card asks to decide `Vary` for "every refusal localized this way". The PR decides "only the `501`s", because "the other localized refusals (`403`, `409`, …) are not" cacheable by default. A `404` is cacheable by default too (RFC 9110 §15.1 lists 404, 405, 410, 414 and 501), and `main` ships one: `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` carries a `userMessage` in the caller's language (`record_not_found`, `packages/core/src/utils/record-not-found.ts:75`), and `GET /data/:object/:id` raises it (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-data-crud.ts:1016`). The caller's locale is the request's `Accept-Language` first. That answer carries no `Vary`, and `Fixes #37737` closes the only card that tracks it. The code on this head is right as far as it goes, so the fix is on the prose faces and does not move the head: file a follow-up card for the localized `404`, correct the sentence in the PR body, and record on card #37737 that item 6 is answered for the `501`s and continues on that card.

N1 (nit) — Card #37737 has no comment that records the split of item 5. The split is readable only from #37811's body, and the card's claim comment still lists the item 5 doors in its file surface. A one-line comment on the card fixes it.

N2 (nit) — The new `requestLocaleOf` jsdoc names `comments.ts`, `webhooks.ts`, `approvals.ts` and `automation-hooks.ts` as modules that read it, and this same diff removes the import from all four. They now reach it through `catalogNotImplemented`. The four gate comments in `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` for those modules likewise still say their `501`s go through `deps.error`. Both are comments in code, so I leave them as an accepted deviation, to be corrected when #37811 next touches these files.

N3 (nit) — The walk's comment says a new bridge is held to the rules "whichever way it is mounted". It finds a module by the two call spellings inside `packages/runtime/src/domains/`, so an aliased import, or a bridge built in another directory, is not walked. Accepted deviation: no such bridge exists on `main`.

Note for #37811, not a finding on this head: the fixed-English `501`s on `main` also include `capabilityUnavailable` (`unavailable.ts`, ten call sites in `ai.ts`, `automation.ts`, `notifications.ts` and `ui.ts`), `share-links.ts:184` and `security.ts:208`. That card's table names none of the three.

This round judges only the fixes made on the prose faces, each re-read from the platform: the PR body, card #37737's new comment 7210847585, the new card #37828, and comment 7210862044 on #37811.

Check-runs on this head: 60 success, 13 skipped, none failed. The PR body edit re-ran `PR-body guards` and `Check Changeset`, and both are green on the edited body.

### ① Derived judgments

Unchanged from record 7210823764: every derived judgment was named right, and the tree is the same. `Fixes #37737` now holds against the card as its comments stand: items 1 to 4 are in the tree, item 5 is on #37811, and item 6 is answered for the ten `501`s with its remainder on #37828.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged. The changeset is not touched. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are still on the PR body's line starts after the edit.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag "Vary goes only on the `501`s".** Answered. The PR body now says the header goes on the ten request-localized `501`s only, and that the localized `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` of `GET /data/:object/:id` is cacheable by default, is not covered here, and is tracked by #37828. The sentence that called the other localized refusals not cacheable is gone.
- **Dev flag "item 4 is closed by widening".** Answered in record 7210823764; unchanged.
- **`open_questions`.** The PR body still carries none.
- **SQL push-down.** Nothing to push down; the diff is the same.

### ④ Design judgment

S1: closed. All three parts of the fix are on the platform, and none moved the head.

- Card #37828 is open and queued. It names the `404`, the two source lines (`record-not-found.ts:75`, `protocol-data-crud.ts:1016`), the missing `Vary`, and a done-when list that also asks whether any other default-cacheable status carries a localized message.
- The PR body's small-call sentence is corrected, as ③ describes.
- Comment 7210847585 on card #37737 records that item 6 is answered for the `501`s only and continues on #37828.

N1: closed. The same comment records that item 5 is split off to #37811 and that the item 5 doors in the claim's file surface are not part of this PR.

N2: accepted deviation, now carried. Comment 7210862044 on #37811 names both stale comments (the `requestLocaleOf` reader list and the four gate comments in `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`) for correction when that card touches the files. The same comment adds the three fixed-English `501` sites my note listed.

N3: accepted deviation, unchanged. No bridge on `main` is mounted in a way the walk misses.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
